title: A Worldling Spent Each Day
description: A Worldling Spent Each Day in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 105, “The rich man and Lazarus. Lk 16:19-25”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A World-ling spent each day In lux-u-ry and state; While a be-liev-er lay, A beg-gar at his gate: Think not the Lord'S ap-point-ments strange, Death made a great and last-ing change.

lines: Think not the Lord'S appointments strange,
Death made a great and lasting change.
And to the land of peace,
From all his pomp and pride
The beggar's bliss from far beheld,
His soul with double anguish filled.
One drop of water I entreat,
To soothe my tongue's tormenting heat."
While the poor beggar pined for food.
With tears he begged his bread;
But now, he weeps no more,
His griefs and pains are fled:
While thine expire in endless woe."
The greatest evil we can fear,
Is to possess our portion here!

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
